Lululemon DOJ OR FTC OR EU competition 2026

findings.claim: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced on 2026-04-13 that his office opened an investigation (civil investigative demand) into Lululemon over whether its athletic apparel contains PFAS ('forever chemicals') that health-conscious customers would not expect given the brand's marketing. Scope: review of the company's Restricted Substances List, testing protocols and supply chain practices against its stated safety standards. Framed as a consumer-protection matter.
findings.source: National Law Review, 'Texas AG Announces CID to Lululemon into PFAS in Athletic Apparel' https://natlawreview.com/article/texas-ag-investigates-lululemon-potential-presence-pfas-activewear ; Freeman Mathis & Gary, 'PFAS regulatory scrutiny expands to consumer apparel: What the Texas AG's Lululemon inquiry signals' https://www.fmglaw.com/environmental-law/pfas-regulatory-scrutiny-expands-to-consumer-apparel-what-the-texas-ags-lululemon-inquiry-signals/

note: Antitrust / monopoly / DOJ / FTC / EU competition: searches returned no investigation, enforcement action or breakup risk against Lululemon (none found, not a confirmation of absence). Only regulatory item found is the Texas AG PFAS inquiry; search results did not show its outcome or any later status update. The September 2026 Pomerantz investor alert concerns securities claims after the 2026-09-03 results, not antitrust. Greenwashing suit reported dismissed in S.D. Fla. (private litigation, per Arnold & Porter blog dated 2025-04), not a government action.
